note: ὁ γνωρίζων is an articular participle; with “knowing” after it, “one who” left a broken clause.
ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ: the preposition gives “before”, so the genitive is simply “him”.
ἐκ νόμου Θεοῦ: the genitive needs “of”, the law of God.
κραυγὴν πτωχῶν: the genitive needs “of”, the cry of the poor.
κατὰ ἔθνους ... κατὰ ἀνθρώπου: κατά with the genitive is against; “according to” lost the sense.
κατὰ ἔθνους ... κατὰ ἀνθρώπου: κατά with the genitive is against; “according to” lost the sense.
λάρυγξ is the throat that tastes food, parallel to the ear that tests words.

grammar: present active participle, nom. masc. sg.
note: βασιλεύων ἄνθρωπον ὑποκριτὴν takes an object: he makes a hypocrite king; “reigning” lost the object.
δυσκολίας λαοῦ: the genitive needs “of”, the perverseness of the people.
ἐνεχυράσω is a first-person future: I will take as pledge; “you took” gave the wrong person and tense.
συνετοὶ καρδίας: καρδίας is a genitive singular, discerning of heart; “hearts” made it a plural noun with no case.
ἐναντίον τοῦ Κυρίου: the preposition gives “before” and τοῦ “the”; “of the Lord” doubled them.
ἑαυτῶν follows the first-person ἑλώμεθα and γνῶμεν: among ourselves, not “their own”.
ἐπισκοπὴ ἀνδρὸς: the genitive is the man who is looked after, oversight of a man.
ἐπισκοπὴ αὐτῷ: the dative gives for whom the care is.
ἕκαστος αὐτῶν is partitive: each of them.
τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν: τίς is “who”; “what kind” is ποῖος.
AD ἀπ᾿ with the accusative ἄνδρα is a misprint for ἐπ᾿, as Athens prints: he will not set it upon a man.
δὲ joins the second clause here; the alternative gloss is resolved to “and”.
δεῖξόν μοι: the dative is the one shown, show to me.
ἀπὸ ὕβρεως πονηρῶν is causal, because of the insolence of the wicked; “before” is not the sense.
ὥς ἐστι is a comparison, as he is; “so as” suggests purpose.
ἡγήσω is aorist: what did you reckon this; the future was wrong.
σὺ τίς εἶ ὅτι εἶπας: ὅτι is consecutive, who are you that you said; it is not causal.
καὶ τοῖς τρισὶ φίλοις σου: the dative is the second recipient of the answer, to the three friends.
ὡς ὑψηλὰ ἀπὸ σοῦ: ὑψηλὰ is a predicate adjective, how high they are; “high places” made it a noun.

grammar: aorist active indicative, second singular, in a rhetorical question
note: εἰ ἥμαρτες is a conditional, if you sinned; “have you sinned” made it a question.
τί πράξεις is a future verb, what will you do; “deeds” read it as a noun.
λήψεται ἐκ χειρός σου is to receive from your hand; “seize” adds force the Greek lacks.
εἰ δὲ καὶ: δὲ is glossed “and”, so καὶ is adverbial “even”; “and and” doubled it.
τῷ προοιμίῳ is already glossed “with the discourse”; “the” on the article doubled it.
Μὴ opens a direct question (has he any boldness before him?); it is not a negation.
δὴ with a future statement (I will declare) is emphatic “indeed”; “please” belongs to requests.
κενὰ κενοῖς: empty things to empty things; κενοῖς is a dative of the same adjective, not “worthless idols”.

grammar: preposition with dative, in one's service
note: παρὰ Παντοκράτορος with the genitive is “from” the Almighty; “with” is the dative sense.
εἰς σφαγὴν ἔσονται: they will be for slaughter, εἰς of destination; “into” is not the sense.
ἐὰν δὲ καὶ: and if even; δὲ is already “and”, so “and and” doubled it.

grammar: verb, aorist subjunctive active, 3rd person plural
note: προσαιτήσουσιν is from προσαιτέω, to beg; “seek” loses the sense.

grammar: noun, dative masculine singular; cognate dative with ἀποθανεῖσθε
note: ἐν θανάτῳ: ἐν (position 5) carries the relation; “by death” doubled it.
κοιμηθήσεται is a statement (the rich man will lie down), not a question.

grammar: adverb / accusative singular masculine of participle used adjectivally modifying implied noun or functioning as predicate adjective in context
note: ὁ πικράνας is an aorist participle, the one who embittered my soul; “bitterly” turned it into an adverb.

grammar: verb, aorist indicative middle, 3rd person singular
note: ὑφείλετο (ὑφαιρέω, middle) is to take away secretly: gloom stole him away; “was being paid” is wrong.

grammar: future middle indicative, 3rd sg., shall take up/bear
note: ἀναλήψεται is will take up; the parenthesis “(up)” is a stray alternative.
ἐπιρρίψει ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν: will cast upon him; the object follows, so “pour upon it” invented an object and a wrong sense.
κροτήσει ἐπ᾿ αὐτοὺς χεῖρας: clap hands at them; ἐπί with the accusative is not “around”.
With ἀπαλλάξω the first μου is a genitive of separation: put away from me my innocence; “my” doubled the following “my”.
οἱ ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ ἐπανιστάμενοι: those rising against me; ἐπί is hostile, not “on”.

grammar: present participle middle masculine nominative/ vocative plural
note: ἐμὲ is already glossed at position 17; “rising up against me” doubled “me”.
τῶν παρανόμων depends on ἀπώλεια: the destruction of the lawless; the genitive article needs “of the”.
ὅτι ἐπέχει explains the hope asked about (what hope, that he holds on?); it gives no cause.
ἦ continues the questions of verse 8 (or will God hear his plea?), as Athens' ἢ shows; “truly” misreads it.

grammar: V aor subj act 1st sg doric
note: AD ἀπολλάξω is a misprint for ἀπαλλάξω (Athens): I will not put away my innocence; “destroy” is wrong.
τῶν ἀσεβῶν is already glossed “of the ungodly”; “the” on the article doubled it.
ἐν θανάτῳ τελευτήσουσι: they will die in death (plague); “among” is the wrong sense of ἐν here.
ἴσα with the dative is “like”: like clay; “as in” invented a relation.
γίνεται here is “comes, is produced”: the place silver (iron) comes from; “becomes” leaves no complement.
δίνας ποταμῶν: eddies of rivers; the genitive after the head noun needs “of”.
αὐτῇ is dative: equal to her (wisdom); “it” dropped the dative and changed the referent.
τὸ ἄλλαγμα αὐτῆς: the exchange for her (wisdom); “it” lost the genitive relation.
γαβὶς is a transliterated word (Athens Γαβεὶς), a precious substance; “a raven” has no basis in the Greek.

grammar: future passive indicative, third singular with genitive
note: μνησθήσεται is passive: lofty things will not be remembered; “will remember” made it active.
ἐκ γῆς: iron is taken from the earth (soil), not from “the land” as a territory.
γίνεται here is “comes, is produced”: the place silver (iron) comes from; “becomes” leaves no complement.
ἐποίησεν is “made, did”; “prepared” belongs to ἑτοιμάζω.
τινάγματι is a shaking (of thunder); ἐν is already glossed, so “in a thing” doubled “in” and lost the sense.
εἶπε ἀνθρώπῳ: he said to man; the dative of the addressee needs “to”.

grammar: noun, nominative fem. sg. coordinated, knowledge
note: ἐπιστήμη is the noun alone; the “and” belongs to δὲ at position 10.

grammar: aorist active indicative, third singular; sexual sense in context
note: ἔγνω is a simple aorist: no bird knew the path; “had known” is pluperfect.
αὐτὴν refers to τρίβος, the path; “her” wrongly personified it (position 9 already has “it”).
ἐκ ῥιζῶν: ἐκ is already “from”; “of roots” added a second relation.
χρυσίῳ ᾿Ωφίρ is the gold of Ophir; the name follows its head noun with “of”, in the familiar form.

grammar: article, nominative neuter singular; introduces substantival participle
note: τὸ ἀπέχεσθαι is an articular infinitive: the keeping away; “what is” invented a clause.
τῷ λάρυγγι ἐκολλήθη: the tongue clung to the throat; the dative needs “to”.
εὐλογία ... ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ ἔλθοι: the blessing came upon me; ἐπί is not hostile here.
ἴσα διπλοΐδι: like a double cloak; ἴσα with the dative is “like”, and “in” was invented.
ὀφθαλμὸς τυφλῶν: the eye of the blind; the genitive needs “of”, as χωλῶν has.
πολὺν χρόνον is a long time; “numerous” cannot qualify a singular “time”.
ὧν (attracted to ἡμερῶν) refers to the days in which God guarded me; “whose” makes it possessive.
δὲ links the two clauses (and they were overjoyed); the alternative “and/but” must be resolved.

grammar: verb, imperfect, indicative, active, 3rd person, plural
note: ἐχέοντο is imperfect middle/passive: my roads were flowing (with butter); “they poured” made the roads agents.

grammar: verb, imperfect, indicative, active, 3rd person, plural
note: ἐχέοντο is imperfect middle/passive: my roads were flowing (with butter); “they poured” made the roads agents.
ὅτε is temporal, continuing the series of “when” clauses; “because” is ὅτι.

grammar: aorist active participle, nominative masculine plural
note: ἐπιθέντες δάκτυλον ἐπὶ στόματι: having put a finger on the mouth; “loaded” is the wrong sense of ἐπιτίθημι.
τῷ προοιμίῳ is already glossed “with the discourse”; “the” on the article doubled it.
ὁ λύχνος is simply the lamp; “the one” invented a pronoun.
τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ is an instrumental dative: by his light I walked through darkness.
ἐχέοντο γάλακτι: the hills were flowing with milk; the dative needs “with”, as βουτύρῳ has.
διπλοΐς is a noun, a double cloak, not the adjective “double”.

grammar: relative pronoun, genitive neuter plural; attracted to antecedent
note: ὧν ... αὐτῶν refers to persons: men whose fathers I despised; “which” made them things and lost the possessive.
οὓς refers to the fathers, persons whom I did not count worthy; “which” is for things.
με is the accusative object of ἐβδελύξαντο: they abhorred me; “to me” invented a dative.
πτύελον is spittle (Athens πτυέλου, saliva); “wing” is wrong.
ὡς βούλεται: as he wills; ὡς here is “as”, not temporal.
ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ ἐκχυθήσεται: my soul will be poured out upon me; ἐπί is not hostile here.
ἴσα πηλῷ: like clay; ἴσα with the dative is “like”, and “in” was invented.
ἐπέβης μοι: you came upon me, the dative of the one attacked; “to me” gave no sense with “set foot”.
παντὶ θνητῷ is dative: a house for every mortal; “all” lost the dative and the singular.
οἰκία ... γῆ: the earth is the house of every mortal; “land” is the wrong sense here.
ἐπὶ παντὶ ἀδυνάτῳ ἔκλαυσα: I wept over every helpless one; ἐπί gives the cause of weeping.
With ἐπί glossed “over”, ἀδυνάτῳ is its noun object; “for the” added a second relation.

grammar: present active participle, nominative masculine singular
note: ἐπέχων ἀγαθοῖς: waiting for good things, as Athens is glossed; “trusting in” is not a sense of ἐπέχω.
ἄνευ φιμοῦ: without a muzzle; φιμός is a muzzle, not “of the mouth”.
ἐν ἐνδείᾳ καὶ λιμῷ: one ἐν governs both nouns (in want and famine); “by” invented a second relation.

grammar: aorist active participle, masculine accusative plural
note: ῥίζας is the noun “roots”, object of ἐμασσῶντο; “gnawing” belongs to the verb.
ῥίζας ξύλων: roots of trees; the genitive needs “of”, and ξύλα here are trees, not wood.
ὧν οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν: whose houses were holes in the rocks; “which” lost the possessive.

grammar: verb, imperfect indicative middle 3rd person plural
note: διῃτῶντο (διαιτάομαι) is to live, pass one's life; “dividing” is wrong.
ἀφρόνων υἱοὶ: sons of fools; the genitive needs “of”.
κατεγέλασάν μου: they laughed at me; μου is the genitive object, not a possessive.
τοῦ προσώπου: the article is glossed at position 8, so “the face” doubled it.
ἐπὶ δεξιῶν βλαστοῦ: on the right of the brood; the genitive needs “of”.
νυκτί is a dative of time: at night my bones are confounded.
οὐκ ἀκούεις μου: you do not hear me; μου is the genitive object, not a possessive.
ἐν ἀνάγκαις: a man in distresses; ἀνάγκη here is hardship, as Athens' “distress”.
ἀρέσαι is the optative of wish, matching ταπεινωθείη: then may my wife please another.
θυμὸς ὀργῆς: the fury of anger; the genitive needs “of”.
ἐκ ῥιζῶν: ἐκ is already “from”; “of roots” added a second relation.
The subject of ἀπώλεσεν is the fire (πῦρ) of the verse; “he” named a person.
κρινομένων αὐτῶν πρός με: when they disputed with me; πρός of a legal dispute is “with”.
ἐπισκοπή here is the Lord's visitation for judgment, parallel to ἔτασις; “watchtower” is wrong.
ἀπόκρισιν ποιήσομαι: what answer will I make; “take” is not the sense.
τῇ αὐτῇ κοιλίᾳ: the article is glossed at position 15, so “the womb” doubled it.
χήρας is genitive singular, depending on τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν: the eye of a widow.
δὲ links the clauses; the alternative “and/but” must be resolved.
ἐκ νεότητός μου: from my youth, parallel to ἐκ γαστρός; “at” is not the sense.

grammar: verb, aorist active participle, masculine vocative singular
note: ὑπερεῖδον is a finite aorist, I overlooked; “having seen” lost both the person and the sense.

grammar: verb, aorist, active, indicative, 2nd person singular
note: ἐπῇρα χεῖρα: I lifted up a hand; “tried” is wrong.
ὀρφανῷ with ἐπῇρα χεῖρα is a dative of disadvantage: raising the hand against the orphan.
πεποιθὼς ὅτι: trusting that great help was at hand; ὅτι gives the content, not a cause.
συνέσχε με: the fear of the Lord held me fast, restrained me; “held together” is the wrong sense.

grammar: particle in ἦ μὴν 'surely' after oath; at 42:16 as printed ἦ μήν
note: ἦ opens a further question (or do I not see the sun?), as Athens' ἢ shows; “surely” misreads it.
λάθρᾳ means secretly; “deceitfully” repeats the verb's idea instead.
χεῖρα ἐπιθεὶς ἐπὶ στόματι: having put my hand on my mouth; “with” is not the sense.
ἐπιχαρὴς πτώματι: glad at the fall; the dative gives the cause of joy and needs “at”.
τῷ ἀδίκῳ is a dative of disadvantage: destruction to the unjust; the bare article lost the relation.
ἀδίκῳ is the adjective “unjust” used as a person, not the noun “wrong”.
τοῖς ποιοῦσιν: to those who do; the participle gloss already has “those”, so the article gives only the dative “to”.
θρυλληθείην ὑπὸ λαοῦ: may I be a byword by (among) my people; ὑπό with the passive marks the agent.
μου χρηστοῦ ὄντος is a genitive absolute: I being very kind; μου is its subject, not a possessive.

grammar: aorist active participle, nominative masculine singular
note: ἁμαρτὼν is an aorist participle of the speaker: having sinned; “who sinned” made it a relative clause.
πολυοχλίαν πλήθους: the crowd of a multitude; the genitive needs “of”.
τίς δῴη is the wish formula (who might give, oh that); “may he give” misreads τίς.
συγγραφὴν ... κατά τινος: a written charge against someone; κατά with the genitive is hostile.
τινος is governed by κατά; “of” added a second relation.
ἐπ᾿ ἐμοὶ ἐστέναξεν: the land groaned against me; ἐπί is hostile here.
μόνος agrees with the speaker (I ate alone); “by himself” put it in the third person.
κυρίου τῆς γῆς: the owner of the land; the genitive article needs “of the”.

grammar: aorist optative active first person singular
note: σπείραιμι is an optative of wish in a self-curse: may I sow and others eat.

grammar: adjective, genitive masculine singular; reciprocal construction
note: ἀνδρὸς ἑτέρου: the wife of another man; the genitive needs “of”.
ἐπὶ θύραις αὐτῆς: lying in wait at her doors; “on” is not the sense.
διαθήκην ἐθέμην τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς: I made a covenant with my eyes; the dative needs “with”.
κρίμα θεράποντός μου: the claim of my servant; the genitive needs “of”.

grammar: aorist indicative active first person singular
note: ἐξέτηξα (ἐκτήκω) is to make melt or waste away: I did not wear out the widow's eye; “cursed” is wrong.
αὐτόν is the naked man; “it” misses the person.
κουρᾶς ἀμνῶν: the fleece of lambs; the genitive needs “of”.
πτώματι ἐχθρῶν: the fall of my enemies; the genitive needs “of”.
AD θαράπαιναί is a misprint for θεράπαιναί (Athens): my maidservants; “the” is already on position 6.
χρηστοῦ is the predicate of the genitive absolute (I being very kind); “of good” misread the genitive.
ἐπ᾿ ἐμοὶ: with ἐπί glossed “against”, ἐμοί is its object; “to” is extra.
ἡσύχασαν ... ἔτι ἀντειπεῖν: they ceased to answer Job any more; with a verb of ceasing ἔτι is “any more”, not “still”.
ἐνωτίζεσθε is an imperative, give ear (ἐνωτίζομαι, from οὖς); “you were being girded” is wrong.
ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων is a genitive absolute: while you listen; ὑμῶν is its subject, not “your”.

grammar: present active participle, genitive masculine plural
note: With ὑμῶν glossed “you”, ἀκουόντων is the participle; “as you listen” doubled “you”.

grammar: demonstrative pronoun, nominative neuter plural; qualitative demonstrative
note: τοιαῦτα ῥήματα: such words; “things like these” doubled the noun ῥήματα.
οὐκ ἀπεκρίθησαν ἔτι: they answered no longer; with a negation ἔτι is “any longer”, not “still”.
ὅτι ἔστησαν gives the reason he waited: because they stood without answering.
πλήρης ῥημάτων: full of words; ῥῆμα is “word”, and the genitive needs “of”.

grammar: personal pronoun, accusative first singular, subject of the preceding infinitive
note: με is the accusative object of ὀλέκει: the spirit destroys me.

grammar: present participle active masculine nominative singular
note: ζέων is to boil, ferment (of new wine); “living” is ζῶν.

grammar: article, nominative masculine singular in an elliptical patronymic
note: AD ὁ is the article of Βουζίτης, the Buzite; “descendant” belongs to ὁ τοῦ with a genitive name, not here.
Βουζίτης is the Buzite, in the familiar English form; the article is glossed at position 7.
ὠργίσθη τῷ Ἰὼβ: he was angry with Job; the dative needs “with”.
δίκαιον ἐναντίον Κυρίου: righteous before the Lord; ἐναντίον is “before”, not “against”.

grammar: preposition governing genitive in expression of shutting the door
note: κατὰ τῶν τριῶν φίλων ὠργίσθη: angry against the three friends; κατά with the genitive is hostile.
ἔθεντο αὐτὸν εἶναι ἀσεβῆ: they set him down to be ungodly; εἶναι is an infinitive, not “being”.
δοῦναι ἀπόκρισιν ᾿Ιώβ: to give an answer to Job; the indeclinable name is the dative of the recipient.

grammar: comparative adjective/noun, nominative masculine plural after οἱ, elders/seniors
note: πρεσβύτεροι ... ἡμέραις is the comparative: older in days, not the office of elders.
αὐτοῦ after the comparative πρεσβύτεροι is a genitive of comparison: older than him.
ἡμέραις is a dative of respect: older in days.
ἐν στόματι τῶν τριῶν ἀνδρῶν: in the mouth of the three men; the genitive article needs “of the”.

grammar: article, nominative masculine singular in an elliptical patronymic
note: AD ὁ is the article of Βουζίτης, the Buzite; “descendant” belongs to ὁ τοῦ with a genitive name, not here.

grammar: nominative singular masculine noun (genitive of place of origin)
note: Βουζίτης is the Buzite, in the familiar English form; “of Bozeth” misread the nominative.

grammar: adjective, nominative masculine plural; substantival, used as address
note: πρεσβύτεροι against νεώτερος is the comparative: you are older; not the office of elders.

grammar: reflexive pronoun, first person genitive masculine singular
note: τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιστήμην: my own knowledge; the reflexive is possessive, not “myself”.

grammar: noun, accusative fem. sg. after τὴν understood
note: ἐπιστήμην is knowledge; the alternative “knowledge/understanding” must be resolved.
σοφοί is the predicate: the long-lived are not wise; “the wise” made it a subject.
μέχρι ὑμῶν συνήσω: I will attend as far as you; ὑμῶν is the object of the preposition, not a possessive.
Κυρίῳ προσθέμενοι: having joined ourselves to the Lord; the dative needs “to”, as Athens has.
τοῦ is already glossed “the”; “the righteous person” repeated the article.
συντελέσουσι τὰς ἡμέρας is active with an object: they will complete their days.
καρδίᾳ is a dative of respect: hypocrites in heart.
ἀποθάνοι is optative, a wish: may their soul die; “he died” gave the wrong mood and subject.
ὑπὸ ἀγγέλων with the passive τιτρωσκομένη gives the agent: wounded by angels.
αὐτῆς refers to ἄβυσσος, a thing: beneath it.
δι᾿ ἀσέβειαν takes the accusative: because of the impiety; “through” is the genitive sense.
ἐδέχοντο is imperfect, they were receiving; “would receive” made it conditional.
μεῖνόν με takes an object: wait for me; “stay!” left με without a relation.
ἐπὶ is already glossed “on”; “of these things” added a second relation.
πᾶς ἄνθρωπος is every man; “all man” is not English.
πολύς of God is great; “numerous” cannot describe one subject.

grammar: future indicative active 3rd person plural middle/passive verb
note: ρυήσονται is from ῥέω, to flow; “will be shaken” is not its sense.
ἐπὶ ἀμυθήτων βροτῶν: βροτῶν agrees with ἀμυθήτων under ἐπὶ, over countless mortals; “of” was invented.
ἐπεκτάσεις νεφέλης: the genitive needs “of”, the spreadings of the cloud.
ριζώματα τῆς θαλάσσης: the genitive article needs “of”, roots of the sea.
δώσει τροφὴν τῷ ἰσχύοντι: the dative is the recipient, to the strong one.
περὶ with the genitive is “concerning”; “for” gives the wrong relation.
αὐτῆς refers to the light he covers: concerning it.
περὶ with the genitive is “concerning”; “for” gives the wrong relation.
περὶ αὐτοῦ: αὐτοῦ is the object of the preposition, concerning him, not “his”.
ἄδικα agrees with ρήματα: unjust words; “wrong things” made a second noun.
τὸν is already glossed “the”; “the innocent” repeated it.
ἰσχύϊ καρδίας: the genitive needs “of”, strength of heart.
τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ ἐτάζων: τίς is “who”, as in the parallel τίς later in the verse.
μεγάλα ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα: the verb links subject and predicate, his works are great.

grammar: noun, genitive neuter plural of age
note: ἀριθμὸς ἐτῶν: the genitive needs “of”, number of years.
AD ἀπεκτάσεις is a one-letter misprint for ἐπεκτάσεις, as Athens prints: the spreadings of the cloud.
ἐν is already glossed “in”; αὐτοῖς is simply “them”.
περὶ with the genitive is “concerning”; “for” gives the wrong relation.
ὡς ἐὰν βούληται: ἐάν stands for ἄν, however he wills; “if” invented a condition.
δύναμιν Κυρίου: the genitive needs “of”, the power of the Lord.
πτώματα πονηρῶν: the genitive plural is the wicked who fall, falls of the wicked.
ὅρασις ἐπιχύσεως: the genitive needs “of”, the look of an outpouring.
πᾶσι is dative: not visible to all.
παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ: αὐτοῦ is the object of the preposition, from him, not “his”.
φοβηθήσονται δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ σοφοὶ: δὲ is glossed “and”, so καὶ is adverbial, even the wise.
τῆς γῆς: the article now carries “of the”, so γῆς is “earth”; “the of the earth” was garbled.
ἐν is already glossed “in”; φωνῇ is simply “a voice”, and “with a voice” doubled the preposition.
συντάσσων χιόνι: the dative is the one commanded, the snow (be on the earth); “with snow” lost the address.
ἐπὶ γῆς: snow falls on the earth, not on a land.
παντὸς ἀνθρώπου: the genitive is whose hand, the hand of every man.
